title: applied-ml-experiment-scratchpad-2026-03-12
content:
Daily scratchpad - focused on quant/quality tradeoffs for the 7B family and prompt stability tests. Quick notes + run log + next steps.

Context: prepping model variants for Redwood Dedicated customers. Goal is to find lowest-cost quant profile (4-bit/8-bit) for redwood-alpha-7b that preserves chat coherence and tool-calling reliability on our eval set (convQA + structured output). Running against prompt-set v3.2 (see sample prompts below).

Summary so far:
- Baseline (fp16, redwood-alpha-7b): PPL ~ 8.9 on convQA-val, instruction-following score 92/100, tool-call parsing success 98%.
- 8-bit static quant (INT8 static): PPL ~ 9.6, instr-score 89/100, tool-call 95%. OK tradeoff for 2.5x throughput improvement.
- 4-bit QLoRA-style (4-bit out + GPTQ attempt): PPL jumped to ~12.4, instr-score 75/100, tool-call 80% - too lossy on structured outputs (parsing mistakes).
- 4-bit with outlier-aware group quant (new kernel): PPL ~10.8, instr-score 83/100, tool-call 90% - promising but still worse than INT8. Need more evals.

Run log (2026-03-11 to 2026-03-12):
- 2026-03-11 09:10: ran baseline fp16 on 1000 convQA-val examples (batch=4) - used dedicated pool in us-west2; notes: KV cache warm-up helps, latency tail 95th 160ms.
- 2026-03-11 13:30: INT8 static quant run (same seed) - batch=8, throughput +2.4x; observed occasional verbatim tokenization issues on long prompts (truncation flags?). File: int8-run-20260311.log (see linked artifact in GH pr).
- 2026-03-12 02:15: attempted 4-bit GPTQ script on alpha-7b (forked from igg/gptq repo) - training diverged on some modules; hypothesize embedding/layernorm sensitivity.
- 2026-03-12 08:40: ran new outlier-aware group-quant code (dev-kernel) - params: group=128, clip=0.002. Partial success.

Prompt set (v3.2) - representative samples: (shortened)
- "Summarize the following customer message and extract (customer_id, issue_type, urgency) in JSON."
- "Given the API trace below, return the minimal set of steps to reproduce the bug."
- "Write a short policy that denies access when X and returns a structured reason code."
Notes: structured-output prompts are very sensitive to subtle changes in token probabilities - quantization seems to hurt the serialized punctuation and spacing.

Failure modes observed:
- Token splitting differences under 4-bit cause trailing commas instead of closing braces in JSON outputs.
- Tool-call arg ordering occasionally swapped (likely beam/search difference w/ quant noise).
- Rare hallucinations at the end of responses when KV cache gets reused across conversations in low-precision kernels.

Hypotheses / experiments to run next:
- H1: Use hybrid quant (8-bit for attention/projection matrices, 4-bit for feed-forward) - might keep structural integrity while improving cost.
  - Plan: implement hybrid bitmask in quant pipeline, run 500-sample convQA subset.
- H2: Per-channel clipping based on activation histograms reduces JSON punctuation errors.
  - Plan: add activation collector to the dev kernel; re-run outlier-aware quant with adaptive clip.
- H3: Prompt engineering (explicit JSON schema + marker tokens) can mitigate some parsing errors even under 4-bit.
  - Plan: test prompt variants: (a) explicit schema with code block delimiters, (b) short schema prefix, (c) delimiter + spacing enforcement.

Immediate TODOs (today):
- [ ] Implement hybrid quant mask in quantize.py (priority P0) - TODO owner: Jordan (blocker: need kernel API changes from infra, ping Rafael).
- [ ] Add activation histogram capture to the instrumented run (owner: Asha) - track per-layer outliers.
- [ ] Run prompt-stability A/B test for v3.2 vs v3.2+schema on 200 examples (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Upload latest dev-kernel binary to GH pr and tag (owner: Jordan).
- [ ] Add regression test for JSON-close punctuation (owner: Jordan) - create unit test that checks for trailing commas/missing braces.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Is there a cheap fallback policy we can apply at runtime when we detect malformed JSON? E.g., run a quick post-formatter that attempts to fix trailing commas - but need to be careful about introducing hallucinated keys.
- How much of the drop in instruction score is due to tokenizer differences vs pure weight quantization? Need ablation where we keep fp16 tokenizer behavior (detokenize/retokenize) but use quant weights.
- If hybrid quant produces acceptable quality, estimate cost reduction: INT8 => ~2.2x cost reduction; hybrid target ~1.6-1.8x. Need to bake into cost model for Dedicated SKU.

Misc notes / minor TODOs:
- Add short note to PR description about KV cache warm-up heuristic (affects tail latency).
- Sync with infra on kernel compilation flags for xformers-optimized matmul.

Quick links:
- sample prompts: /confluence/applied-ml/prompt-sets/v3.2
- run artifacts: s3://redwood-inference-logs/quant-runs/2026-03-12/

End of scratchpad.

(Will clean up and lift items into a formal PR checklist after hybrid quant experiments.)
